flaw_triggers.visited_missing: Infinite loop or duplicate vertex visits caused by missing or late visited-set update.
flaw_triggers.queue_order: Vertices popped in LIFO rather than FIFO order.
flaw_triggers.zero_vertex_unhandled: Failure on disconnected components or single vertex.

reference_solution.python:
from collections import deque
def bfs_traversal(V: int, adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    visited = [False] * V
    queue = deque([0])
    visited[0] = True
    result = []
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        result.append(node)
        for neighbor in adj[node]:
            if not visited[neighbor]:
                visited[neighbor] = True
                queue.append(neighbor)
    return result

title: BFS Time and Space Complexity Analysis
description: What is the worst-case time complexity of Breadth-First Search on a graph with V vertices and E edges represented using an Adjacency List?
explanation: BFS visits every vertex once (O(V)) and explores each edge once in directed graph or twice in undirected graph (O(E)). Thus time complexity is O(V + E).

title: Cycle Detection Mechanism
description: In an undirected graph BFS, when can we conclude that a cycle exists?
options: When we encounter any visited vertex regardless of parent.
When an adjacent node is already visited and is NOT the parent of the current node.
When the queue size exceeds V.
When the degree of any vertex is greater than 2.
explanation: If an adjacent vertex is already visited and is not the immediate parent from which we came, it indicates an alternate path / back-edge, proving a cycle.
